items.english: Mr., Mrs., Ms., Miss (more polite than さん)
items.note: Suffix — attaches after a person's name; more formal/polite than さん (san).
さま (sama) is more polite than さん (san) — used for customers, guests, or in formal business address, not with someone you know casually.
The plain adjective inside Lesson 8's いいですね (ii desu ne, 'That's good') — いい alone just means 'nice, good.'
items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 10: Describing Things: It’s Delicious (いい is formally taught as part of the い-adjective class (with its irregular よくないです conjugation called out) only in chapter 29's い-adjectives vocabulary set — here it's used as a bare vocab item ahead of that)

items.note: The same ね as Lesson 6's かいぎは１じからですね (kaigi wa ichiji kara desu ne) — softens a statement and invites agreement, like English 'right?'
items.reviewNote: Source gloss only cross-references Lesson 6 Notes 2 ('particle; see L6, NOTES 2, p. 51'); note content added for learner usability. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 6: Going Places (1): Where Are You Going? (matched on target)

items.note: This lesson's frequency scale, most to least: いつも (itsumo, 'always') > よく (here) > ときどき (tokidoki, 'sometimes') > あまり…ません (amari, 'not often') > ぜんぜん…ません (zenzen, 'not at all').
Middle of this lesson's frequency scale — see よく (yoku, 'often') for the full ranking from いつも down to ぜんぜん.

items.english: (particle marking the person or thing an action is directed at)
items.scene: marking who a call, e-mail or greeting is aimed at
items.note: Marks the person or thing an action targets (あいます 'meet', おしえます 'tell', おくります 'send') — a different job from Lesson 6's に marking where movement ends (ぎんこうにいきます) and Lesson 7's に marking a point in time (げつようびに).
items.reviewNote: Source gloss only cross-references GRAMMAR 1, 2, p. 85. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 2: Possession: Whose Pen Is This? (matched on target)

items.note: Takes に (ni) for the person met, as in たなかさんにあいます — not と (to, 'with') from Lesson 6, which marks doing something together.

items.hint: the whole question you say back when surprised

items.scene: attached to what a shop sells, naming the shop
items.note: Suffix — attaches after a food or goods name to mean 'the shop that sells it,' e.g. てんぷらや (tenpuraya), 'tempura restaurant.'
てんぷら (tempura) + や (ya, shop/restaurant suffix).
Same root as Lesson 2's おしえてください (oshiete kudasai, 'please tell me'); the person told is marked by に, not を.
まい (mai, 'every') + にち (nichi, 'day'). The same まい prefix appears on まいあさ (maiasa, 'every morning'), まいばん (maiban, 'every evening'), and まいしゅう (maishū, 'every week') below.
Used together with a negative verb ending (あまり…〜ません). See: エマさんは あまり テレビを みません (Emma-san does not watch television very often).

items.target: スミスさんはあしたたなかさんにあいます

items.english: Smith-san told Suzuki-san the location of the restaurant.
items.target: スミスさんはすずきさんにレストランのばしょをおしえました
スミスさんはまいにちコーヒーをのみます

items.english: Emma-san does not watch television very often.
items.note: あまり (amari) pairs with a negative verb ending to mean 'not very often, not very'.
items.target: エマさんはあまりテレビをみません

items.note: Follows Lesson 8's [noun]を[します] pattern (テニスをします, tenisu o shimasu); the person called is marked by に, not を — スミスさんはたなかさんにでんわをします.
Like あいます (aimasu, 'meet') and おしえます (oshiemasu, 'tell') above, the recipient is marked by に, not を — スミスさんはたなかさんにメールをおくります.

items.hint: getting information from a person, not listening to audio
items.note: Same target as Lesson 8's ききます (kikimasu), 'listen to' — this one means asking a question, and takes に for the person asked (だれにききますか), not the thing heard.
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 8: Doing Things (1): I’m Going to Eat Tempura (matched on target)

items.scene: politely referring to someone else's family member
items.hint: attaches before a noun like かぞく (family) or しゅじん (husband)
items.note: A different ご (go) from this lesson's language suffix (にほんご, nihongo, 'Japanese') — same sound, unrelated: this one is a prefix showing respect for someone else's things, e.g. ごかぞく (gokazoku).
items.reviewNote: Written ご〜 in the source. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 1: Meeting: Nice to Meet You (matched on english)

items.note: ご (go, honorific prefix) + かぞく (kazoku, 'family') from Lesson 6 — the plain かぞく there was neutral; this ご- form is specifically about someone else's family, never your own.
The everyday word for one's own father is ちち (chichi) — see that card.
The everyday word for one's own mother is はは (haha) — see that card.
Someone else's wife — for your own wife, use つま (tsuma) below, never おくさん about yourself.
Used for one's own father; when talking about someone else's father, use おとうさん (otousan) instead.
Used for one's own mother; when talking about someone else's mother, use おかあさん (okaasan) instead.
Also read かない (kanai) — both mean 'my wife'; use おくさん (okusan) for someone else's wife.
Someone else's husband — for your own husband, use おっと (otto) below, never ごしゅじん about yourself.
Also read しゅじん (shujin) — both mean 'my husband'; use ごしゅじん (goshujin) for someone else's husband.
まい (mai, 'every') + あさ (asa, 'morning') — see まいにち (mainichi, 'every day') above for the pattern.
まい (mai, 'every') + ばん (ban, 'evening') — see まいにち (mainichi, 'every day') above for the pattern.
まい (mai, 'every') + しゅう (shū) — the same しゅう as Lesson 6's せんしゅう (last week), こんしゅう (this week), らいしゅう (next week).
The top of this lesson's frequency scale — see よく (yoku, 'often') for the full ranking down to ぜんぜん (zenzen, 'not at all').

items.hint: the adverb that forces a negative verb after it
items.note: Used with a negative verb ending (ぜんぜん…〜ません); the bottom of this lesson's frequency scale — see よく (yoku, 'often') for the full ranking.

items.english: Emma-san does not drink coffee at all.
items.reviewNote: The chapter glosses ぜんぜん…〜ません but never uses it in a full example sentence; added to show the pattern, reusing コーヒー and のみます from KS3.
items.target: エマさんはぜんぜんコーヒーをのみません
スミスさんはたなかさんにでんわをします
スミスさんはたなかさんにメールをおくります

items.scene: naming a language after a country name
items.hint: attaches after a country's name, not before a noun
items.note: A different ご (go) from this lesson's honorific prefix (ごかぞく, gokazoku) — same sound, unrelated: this one names a language, attaching after a country's name.
items.reviewNote: Written 〜ご in the source. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 2: Possession: Whose Pen Is This? (matched on target)

items.note: にほん (Nihon, Japan) + ご (go, language).

items.target: スミスさんはだれにでんわをしますか
なかむらさんにします

items.target: スミスさんはどこにメールをおくりますか

items.english: He'll send it to the bank.
items.scene: answering where Smith-san will send the e-mail
items.target: ぎんこうにおくります

items.reviewNote: Used repeatedly in this chapter's example sentences (EX III, IV, X) but never given its own vocabulary entry. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 2: Possession: Whose Pen Is This? (matched on target)

items.english: Smith-san asked Nakamura-san for his phone number.
items.note: ききます (kikimasu, 'ask') vs おしえます (oshiemasu, 'tell') below — same でんわばんごう(を) pattern, opposite direction of information.
items.target: スミスさんはなかむらさんにでんわばんごうをききました

items.english: Nakamura-san told Smith-san his phone number.
items.note: Contrasts with the previous card: ききます (kikimasu) 'ask' vs おしえます (oshiemasu) 'tell' — same でんわばんごう(を) pattern, opposite direction of information.
items.target: なかむらさんはスミスさんにでんわばんごうをおしえました

items.english: Smith-san will meet Suzuki-san at Tokyo station at 4:00 on Monday.
items.note: Adds this lesson's target-marking に to the established word order: person は — day/time に — place で — target に — verb, stacking three に's with different jobs in one sentence.
items.target: スミスさんはげつようびの４じにとうきょうえきですずきさんにあいます
items.reading: スミスさんはげつようびのよじにとうきょうえきですずきさんにあいます

items.note: Follows Lesson 8's [noun]を[します] pattern (テニスをします, tenisu o shimasu) — さんぽ (sanpo, 'walk') supplies the activity.

items.english: Kato-san takes a walk every day.
items.target: かとうさんはまいにちさんぽをします

items.english: Sapporo (city on the island of Hokkaido)

items.note: やさい (yasai, vegetable) + ジュース (juusu, juice).

items.scene: answering whether Smith-san often reads books

items.hint: a wine glass specifically, not the everyday コップ from Lesson 5
items.note: A stemmed glass, typically for wine, unlike the everyday tumbler-type コップ (koppu) from Lesson 5 — English 'glass' covers both, Japanese distinguishes them.
ほん (hon) here counts bottles of beer — the same long-object counter from Lesson 5 (ワインを２ほん), just extended to beer.
items.target: ビールを２ほんおねがいします
items.reading: ビールをにほんおねがいします

items.note: A general 'next time' — unlike Lesson 6's specific らいしゅう (next week), らいげつ (next month), らいねん (next year), こんど doesn't say which unit of time.

items.english: What will you do next weekend?
items.target: こんどのしゅうまつになにをしますか

items.english: I will go to the Shibuya Library.
items.scene: answering what Emma will do next weekend
items.target: しぶやとしょかんにいきます

items.english: Do you often go to the Shibuya Library, Emma-san?
items.target: エマさんはよくしぶやとしょかんにいきますか

items.scene: answering whether Emma often goes to the Shibuya Library

items.hint: used for an item, not a person
items.note: The same こちら as Lesson 1's polite word for 'this person,' but here extended to polite これ (for things) — shop staff use it either way, e.g. こちらです ('here you are').
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 1: Meeting: Nice to Meet You (matched on target)

items.note: お (o, honorific prefix) + のみもの (nomimono, beverage); the お is often included in polite speech, e.g. by restaurant staff.
お (o, honorific prefix) + かいけい (kaikei, bill/check).
Said in a restaurant when each person wants to pay their own share, e.g. べつべつに おねがいします ('separately, please').
